symbols.name: lang_report
symbols.note: Local variable; dict mapping language to support status.

claims.text: NEVER a numeric 0: the tree-sitter path has no class/field vocabulary, so 'we did not look' must not read as 'we looked and found none'. Stufe 1 is Python only.
claims.why: The code sets lang_report[lang] = 'not_supported' for non-python languages, never a numeric 0. The comment about 'Stufe 1' is a claim about external context; it is uncheckable in this chunk, but the code does not contradict it.

observations.what: lang_report is initialised with 'python': 'supported' then overridden for non-python languages. If languages dict is empty, no non-python entries are added, so only 'python' key exists.
sorted(languages or {}) sorts keys of languages dict. If languages is None, it becomes empty dict, sorting works. But if languages is a list or other iterable, it may raise TypeError.
